title: Capacity Optimizer: continuous fleet fit classifier, real-time utilization feed, and prescriptive actions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight 'Capacity Optimizer' service that continuously classifies tenant workloads into fit categories (overprovisioned / right-sized / underprovisioned), emits a Real-Time Utilization Feed (RTUF) for the Console and autoscaler, and surfaces prescriptive actions (resize suggestions, burst lanes, and config knobs) to reduce cost while preserving throughput SLOs.

Context: customers running Dedicated pools struggle to balance cost and headroom. Existing reports are batch-oriented and reactive. This ticket introduces a continuously updated fit signal and automated prescriptive recommendations that are safe to surface to operators and product (with manual approval flows).

Scope: schema for RTUF (per-tenant + per-pool), fit-classifier heuristics and ML-lite rules, a recommendations engine (prescriptor) with explainability fields, Console integrations (recommendations list + acceptance actions), and minimal autoscaler hooks (recommendation->suggested autoscale policy change). Excludes full autopilot acceptance — that will be follow-up.

Outcomes: reduced committed spend for pilot tenants, clearer operational runbooks for resizing, and observable regression detection when recommendations increase SLO risk.
acceptance_criteria: RTUF stream is emitted every 5m and contains tenant_id, pool_id, utilization_pct_95, median_latency_ms, tail_latency_ms, kv-cache-hit-rate, model_mix_signature, and fit_score
Fit-classifier produces stable categories (over, right, under) with documented heuristics and unit tests covering corner cases
Prescriptor returns up to 3 ranked actions per tenant with estimated cost delta and risk explanation
Console shows recommendations page with filters, reasoning snippets, and a link to a one-click resize PR template
Integrations: a flag-based hook available to autoscaler to consume recommendations; no automatic enforcement by default
Metrics: new monitoring dashboard with adoption metrics and A/B test for recommended vs. baseline tenants
implementation_notes: Data sources: metrics from runtime telemetry (per-request size/latency), allocator logs (slot packing), and billing aggregates
Fit-classifier approach: start with deterministic rules (utilization bands, tail latency delta, median vs. tail, sustained vs. bursty), then iterate with a small logistic regression model if needed
RTUF schema: lightweight JSON lines shipped to PubSub/Kafka topic 'rtuf.dedicated.v1' with retention 72h for backfills
Prescriptor scoring: cost_delta_estimate computed from historical token/scheduling cost curves; risk_score derived from recent SLO violation probability
Safety: recommendations include 'confidence' and 'canary steps' (e.g., reduce commit by 10% with 24h guardrail), and require manual approval in Console for production tenants
Privacy: tenant identifiers must be hashed for any external analytics exports; internal topics remain access-controlled
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): wire RTUF from staging runtime to staging Console, validate schema and unit tests (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (pilot): enable RTUF for 5 pilot customers; run prescriptor in read-only mode for 3 weeks and collect acceptance signals (cost delta, latency regressions)
Phase 2 (opt-in): surface recommendations in Console for 50 customers behind an opt-in flag; allow manual apply via PR template and telemetry collection (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (enterprise): add autoscaler hook and policy suggestion API; document runbook and offer as beta to enterprise customers (post-approval)
Rollback: all recommendations are reversible and include timeline; if SLO regressions > threshold, automatically retract recent actions and notify oncall
metrics_and_alerts: Adoption: % of pilot tenants that accept at least one recommendation within 14 days
Effectiveness: mean cost_delta_realized and median latency change after applied actions
Safety: number of SLO violations in 48h window post-apply compared to baseline
Data health: RTUF missing-rate per pool > 5% triggers alert
Prescriptor confidence drop: sudden drop in model/confidence triggers review workflow
